📋 Executive summary in-progress **Build phase complete for mbp-01 and mbp-02; ready for Evaluate tooling.** Reviewer feedback through 2026-05-28 is processed (digest + raw export…

Puts the v2ecoli single-cell model inside a bench-scale bioreactor. Seven studies build up the coupling: a time-varying environment hook, population aggregation with representative-sampling scaling, BiRD reactor coupling, multigeneration runs, a sim-vs-Beulig comparison, gap analysis, and a Millard 2017 kinetic-metabolism drop-in with 3-arm Beulig report cards.

in-progress Current verdict. **Build phase complete for mbp-01 and mbp-02; ready for Evaluate tooling.** Reviewer feedback through 2026-05-28 is processed (digest + raw export under `references/expert/`): all 9 inline cleanup items closed in source, the §11 framework root cause seeded as an upstream pbg-superpowers gap, and the two architectural blockers Chris's first pass left open (env-store-topology + env-driver-molecule-id) resolved 2026-05-29 by the EnvironmentMirror Step (commit `60cdbd3`). mbp-01 went from 1 passing / 5 skipped to **6 passing / 0 skipped**.

Question. Can v2ecoli be migrated and enhanced to run inside a bench-scale bioreactor? The pieces are a time-varying external-environment hook, a population aggregator with representative-sampling scaling, and a coupling adapter to `pbg-bioreactordesign`'s BiRDTransportProcess; the test is a structured sim-vs-published comparison report (overlay panels plus divergence triage feeding mbp-06 gap analysis) against the WT batch-phase prefix of the 2025 Beulig/Palsson mSystems study.

Reframed 2026-05-26 per chris_feedback_2026_05_26 §1 + §10: the original "reproduces ... within per-metric tolerances" framing built the tune-to-tolerance impulse into the test design. Success is now defined as "comparison harness built and applied; structured gap inventory produced," not "Palsson benchmark achieved" — all biological divergences feed mbp-06 as evidence.

Hypothesis. Yes, with scope caveats. v2ecoli's Layer-1 Steps (`media_update`, `exchange_data`) already expose the environment-coupling surface and the metabolism Process already emits `external_exchange_fluxes`, so the enhancements are small and additive: (1) a time-varying-env hook over the existing static-medium plumbing, (2) a population aggregator whose `cells_per_agent` representative-sampling scaling derives reactor-scale biomass / OD from per-cell mass listeners, (3) a ReactorCellCoupler Step bridging to `pbg-bioreactordesign`'s BiRDTransportProcess (transport-only fork, no internal biomass ODE by construction — the Option-B decision in chris_feedback_2026_05_26 §5). Each study's acceptance tests gate its impl PR, the multi-generation coupled run checks that no piece drifts over time, and mbp-05's evaluation phase renders the comparison report against Beulig batch-phase trajectories.

Scope caveat: Beulig 2025 reached 50–80 gDW/L (~10^12 – 10^13 cells/L), which v2ecoli's single-cell-with-Division population cannot reach by literal-sum aggregation — hence the `cells_per_agent` scaling factor (mbp-02; representative-sampling under the 0D well-mixed assumption) that lets the simulated lineage stand in for a larger population. mbp-05 is an evaluation phase rendering overlays plus categorized divergences rather than asserting tolerance-based agreement with Beulig, bounding the AI-agent scope to "execute and report" rather than "tune until match"; mbp-06's gap analysis is expected to surface a coarse-grained surrogate engine (under the same cell-side interface contract) as a top-priority follow-up.

🧬 Biology — the mechanism this investigation models A whole-cell model simulates one E. coli cell in molecular detail; a bioreactor runs 10^12–10^13 cells per litre under a changing physical environment — depleting glucose,…

A whole-cell model simulates one E. coli cell in molecular detail; a bioreactor runs 10^12–10^13 cells per litre under a changing physical environment — depleting glucose, oxygen-transfer-limited dissolved O2, accumulating acetate and CO2. This investigation asks whether the single-cell model can be lifted into that bench-scale context and held up against a real published high-density run (Beulig 2025, mSystems; senior author Palsson). The biology is multi-scale: a single lineage's nutrient uptake and growth must aggregate into population-scale biomass, which then draws down the shared medium and consumes oxygen faster than the reactor can transfer it, driving substrate- and O2-limited growth. v2ecoli already exposes the right surfaces (Layer-1 media/exchange Steps, per-cell mass listeners), so the enhancements are additive: an externally driven environment (mbp-01), a representative-sampling population aggregator (mbp-02), and a coupler to the reactor's transport physics (mbp-03).

The central result so far is a scale gap, not a tuning failure. v2ecoli's single-lineage population plateaus at ~4.3 mg/L while the Beulig batch phase peaks at ~9.6 g/L (max OD ~28 × 0.34 gDW/OD), a ~3.3-order gap not closable by run duration or a division-flag flip. True both-daughters accumulation (2^N cells after N generations) needs a population-runner architecture distinct from the current single-lineage runner, and reaching the paper's 50–80 gDW/L additionally needs fed-batch operations. The investigation was therefore reframed (2026-05-26) from "match Beulig within tolerance" to "build the comparison harness and produce a structured gap inventory": every biological divergence becomes evidence feeding mbp-06, not a knob to turn.

🔬 Scientific argument 6 for · 3 against v2ecoli can be additively enhanced (time-varying environment + representative-sampling population aggregation + a BiRDTransportProcess coupler) to…

Main claim. v2ecoli can be additively enhanced (time-varying environment + representative-sampling population aggregation + a BiRDTransportProcess coupler) to operate inside a bench-scale bioreactor and render a structured, reviewable sim-vs-published comparison, with the gap to the Beulig high-density regime attributed to population-runner architecture and fed-batch operations (surfaced as gaps) rather than tuned away.

Caveats

  • mbp-05/mbp-06 are evaluation phases (chris_feedback_2026_05_26 §10) that execute-and-report, deliberately not tolerance-based biology claims.
  • Scope is the batch portion of the Beulig dataset only; fed-batch operations are not yet exposed by pbg-bioreactordesign and are deferred (expected top-priority mbp-06 gap).
  • cells_per_agent is representative sampling under a 0D well-mixed assumption; it lets one simulated lineage stand in for a larger population and does not model spatial heterogeneity.

Overview

This study asks whether can v2ecoli's `media_update` / `exchange_data` Layer-1 Steps consume an. We recorded 1 novel computational result. Gate decision: In progress. Continue analysing run outcomes.

Purpose & background (study design)
Question. Can v2ecoli's `media_update` / `exchange_data` Layer-1 Steps consume an externally-driven, time-varying nutrient pool — instead of the static media configuration baked into ParCa — such that metabolic exchange fluxes and growth rate respond correctly to declining glucose, declining DO, and other dynamic external concentrations?
Mechanism / Model change. v2ecoli's baseline composite currently treats the external environment as a constant medium definition (constrained / unconstrained exchange sets parameterized at composite-build time, see v2ecoli/steps/media_update.py and metabolism's `exchange_data_from_media` method). For reactor coupling, the external pool must be a TIME-VARYING store that external physics writes into each timestep. This study introduces an `EnvironmentDriver` Step (or a thin extension to `media_update`) that reads from an `environment.external_concentrations` store (`map[float]`, mM) and updates the constraints feeding metabolism each step. Reactor / BiRD coupling (mbp-03) writes to that store; this study verifies the plumbing in isolation by driving it with synthetic trajectories.
Expected outcome. **mbp-01 is a PLUMBING study only** (per chris_feedback_2026_05_26 §3 + investigation `discipline.scope_discipline`). It verifies that the store→constraint wire works under extreme/saturating inputs that are robust to v2ecoli's internal transport-kinetics functional form (saturable MM / constant-bound / linear). Quantitative biological- fidelity (gradient shape, μ response to glucose decline near Km, acetate flux shift at sub-Vmax DO) is DEFERRED to a downstream `transport-kinetics-fidelity` study — a candidate-future-study under mbp-06 axis A.

Concretely under this study: - External-concentration changes propagate to metabolism's exchange constraint within one timestep (plumbing wire). - Cumulative mass balance closes (no leakage in the env-driver wire). - With external glucose held at 0, glucose exchange flux ≈ 0. Same for DO at zero. Universal biological floor; plumbing-confirming. - With external glucose at 5 g/L vs 50 g/L (both far above PTS Km), glucose uptake plateaus within ratio 0.9–1.1 (discriminates physical saturable/constant-bound implementations from unphysical linear scaling). - With external glucose at saturating 50 g/L, glucose uptake ≤ published Vmax ceiling for E. coli glucose-PTS (~10–12 mmol/gDW/h). - Static-medium regression unchanged.

Model changes

Internal v2ecoli enhancement — the smallest viable hook that lets external physics drive v2ecoli's metabolism. Implementation must keep the static-medium path untouched for existing baseline regressions (verified by the static-env-regression sim above).

Technical detailsbase_model: v2ecoli.composites.ecoli_baseline
new_state_variables: ["environment.external_concentrations (map[float], mM) — populated by external physics each timestep"]
new_processes: [{"name":"EnvironmentDriver","kind":"Step","requirement_id":"req-1-env-driver"}]
new_parameters: [{"name":"env_driver_mode","default":"external_store","units":"{static|external_store|synthetic_trajectory}"},{"name":"env_driver_trajectory_spec","default":null,"units":"—"}]
modified_processes: ["media_update / exchange_data: read external_concentrations (when env_driver_mode != static) instead of static media config. Backward-compatible default."]

Key assumptions

  • v2ecoli's metabolism Process can re-read environment constraints every step (it already does via `exchange_data_from_media`).
  • External concentrations are well-mixed (single value per species across all agents in this single-cell study).
  • No timestep mismatch handled this phase — env updates and metabolism updates run on the same timebase.

Limitations

  • PLUMBING-ONLY scope (per chris_feedback_2026_05_26 §3). Gradient-shape and quantitative-biological-fidelity tests (e.g. μ response to glucose decline near Km, acetate flux shift at sub-Vmax DO, GUR-vs-[glucose] curve) are deferred to a `transport-kinetics-fidelity` candidate-future-study under mbp-06 axis A.
  • REMOVED tests with rationale (kept here so future agents don't re-add them by reflex): `uptake-flux-tracks-external-glucose` (Pearson ≥ 0.7 assumed linear response; real PTS is saturable, ~3 orders of magnitude above the sweep range — test fails on every realistic implementation). `low-do-clamp-reduces-o2-uptake` (5 µM DO clamp is 25-200× above cytochrome bd/bo3 Km, so OUR shouldn't reduce at this clamp; Vemuri 2006 supports acetate-RISE under low DO, not OUR-drop — citation/test mismatch). `mu-drops-when-glucose-depletes` (kinetics-dependent; defer to transport-kinetics-fidelity study).
  • Single cell only; population aggregation is mbp-02's job.
  • Reactor physics (kLa, gas transport) not coupled here — that is mbp-03.
  • Time-varying-medium support assumes the same exchange-molecule set as static medium; new species require ParCa regeneration.

Overview

This study asks whether can v2ecoli aggregate single-cell-plus-Division output into population-. We recorded 1 novel computational result. Gate decision: In progress. Continue analysing run outcomes.

Purpose & background (study design)
Question. Can v2ecoli aggregate single-cell-plus-Division output into population- level biomass observables (total gDW, cell count) that are physically meaningful at the reactor scale (OD ≫ 1) — using a **representative- sampling scaling factor (`cells_per_agent`)** so the simulated lineage legitimately stands in for an N-cell population under the 0D well-mixed assumption — and consume population-level signals (e.g. reactor liquid volume) to maintain correct concentrations?
Mechanism / Model change. v2ecoli currently tracks `agents.<id>.listeners.mass.cell_mass` per cell and grows the population via the Division Step. There is no built-in aggregation of the population into reactor-scale observables. This study adds a `PopulationAggregator` Step that, each emit step, walks `agents.*.listeners.mass.cell_mass` and writes:

population.total_biomass_gDW = sum(agents.*.cell_mass) × cells_per_agent × 1e-15 g/fg population.cell_count = len(agents) × cells_per_agent population.biomass_concentration_gL = total_biomass_gDW / reactor_volume_L population.OD600 = biomass_concentration_gL / od_to_gdw (COSMETIC — for plotting / cross-referencing OD-only published data)

The `cells_per_agent` factor is the load-bearing architectural decision in this study (adopted 2026-05-26 per chris_feedback_2026_05_26 §4, Eran's choice between literal-sum and representative-sampling). Under the 0D well-mixed assumption (already a key_assumption), every cell sees the same environment, so simulating N representative cells and scaling by k = cells_per_agent is mathematically equivalent to simulating N × k cells. You downsample for compute tractability. Cost: per-cell stochastic variance washes out at the bulk mean as k grows — at high density this is correct biology (population averages dominate over per-cell variance). At low density (small k = 1.0, default), behavior is identical to literal-sum.

Production runs choose `cells_per_agent` such that `n_simulated_agents × cells_per_agent ≈ target_population_density × reactor_volume`. Default 1.0 preserves literal-sum so existing single-cell sims and the unaggregated baseline regression test remain byte-identical.

A `ReactorVolume` external store (read-only here, written by mbp-03's BiRD coupling) determines concentration units. Concentration-to-count conversions in metabolism stay per-cell; only the AGGREGATE view is new.

**`population.OD600` is COSMETIC** — derived from biomass_concentration_gL for plotting and for comparisons against published OD-only data (e.g. Beulig 2025 OD traces). The canonical biomass observable is `population.biomass_concentration_gL` (or `total_biomass_gDW`); downstream studies should NOT reach for OD as the primary biomass currency. Static od_to_gdw = 0.34 (Beulig's value, not the textbook 0.33) is acceptable under this framing; regime-dependence applies to OD interpretation, not to the model's internal biomass accounting.
Expected outcome. cell_count tracks Division events (1 → 2 → 4 → … on a generational cadence ≈ 60 min), scaled by cells_per_agent. total_biomass_gDW grows exponentially during glucose-replete growth, scaled by cells_per_agent. Per-cell observables (e.g. DnaA count) remain unchanged from the unaggregated baseline — aggregation is a read-only view.

Pure consistency invariants hold at every emit step: population.cell_count == len(agents.*) × cells_per_agent population.total_biomass_gDW == sum(agents.*.listeners.mass.cell_mass) × cells_per_agent × 1e-15

These checks are decoupled from doubling-time calibration — they isolate aggregator bugs from biology drift.

Model changes

Read-only aggregation; does NOT modify per-cell state. The Division Step is unchanged. The reactor_volume_L parameter is a default for this phase; mbp-03 will replace it with the reactor composite's dynamic volume store.

cells_per_agent is the load-bearing knob; see purpose.mechanism for the rationale. The cell-side interface contract will be amended in a follow-up edit to reference the scaling discipline as part of the interface — engines either operate at literal scale or declare an explicit cells_per_agent factor.

Technical detailsbase_model: v2ecoli.composites.ecoli_baseline
new_state_variables: ["population.total_biomass_gDW (float)","population.cell_count (float) # float, not int — cells_per_agent scaling can be non-integer","population.biomass_concentration_gL (float) # CANONICAL biomass observable","population.OD600 (float) # COSMETIC — derived from biomass_concentration_gL for plotting / OD-only comparisons"]
new_processes: [{"name":"PopulationAggregator","kind":"Step","requirement_id":"req-1-population-aggregator"}]
new_parameters: [{"name":"cells_per_agent","default":1,"units":"real cells per simulated agent"},{"name":"od_to_gdw","default":0.34,"units":"gDW/(L·OD600)"},{"name":"reactor_volume_L","default":1,"units":"L"},{"name":"fg_per_gram","default":"1e-15","units":"g/fg"}]

Key assumptions

  • Population is well-mixed (all agents see the same reactor liquid). This assumption is what makes the cells_per_agent representative-sampling factor mathematically equivalent to literal-N simulation.
  • Per-cell stochastic variance becomes negligible at large cells_per_agent (correct biology at high density; explicit cost of the representative-sampling choice — see chris_feedback_2026_05_26 §4).
  • od_to_gdw = 0.34 gDW/(L·OD600) per Beulig 2025 (was textbook 0.33).
  • cell_mass listener units are fg (femtograms) per v2ecoli convention.
  • PopulationAggregator runs as a Step at emit cadence; no need for inter-process synchronization.
  • OD600 is a COSMETIC observable (for plotting / OD-only data comparison); biomass_concentration_gL is canonical.

Limitations

  • All agents share the same external environment in this phase (no per-cell microenvironment heterogeneity).
  • OD600 conversion is a constant factor; physical OD depends on cell size + scattering — may need regime-dependent refit (Beulig 2025 high-density regime). Less load-bearing now that OD600 is cosmetic.
  • Aggregator runs at emit cadence; not suitable as a feedback signal to processes that need sub-step granularity (deferred).
  • cells_per_agent scaling washes per-cell stochastic variance at large k — correct biology at high density (population averages dominate), but at k ~ 10-100 may obscure biologically-interesting per-cell heterogeneity (e.g. Beulig 2025's bistable expression states). Setting k is a calibration decision per investigation; see open_question scaling-factor-sets-stochastic-floor.
  • Single-cell-with-Division at small cells_per_agent does not scale to reactor densities (~10^13 cells/L at 50–80 gDW/L) by literal-N simulation. The scaling factor lets the SIMULATED N stand in for a larger M = N × k, sufficient for batch-phase work but with the stochastic-floor caveat above. A coarse-grained surrogate engine under the cell-side interface contract remains the path forward for the full high-density regime (mbp-06 scope; see candidate-future-study `mbp-08-surrogate-engine-for-high-density`).

Model

🧬 reactor_bird_coupleddefault parameters

Biology

Four-way coupling: (1) population biomass -> reactor.biomass; (2) dissolved O2/CO2 (mg/L->mM) -> v2ecoli environment; (3) aggregated metabolism O2 uptake -> BiRD O2 demand; (4) metabolism CO2 production -> BiRD CO2 demand. Expected biology: DO drops below Henry saturation as cells consume O2; dissolved CO2 rises above saturation; higher kLa raises DO and strips CO2; no-cells runs reach Henry equilibrium.

Overview

This study asks whether can v2ecoli (with the mbp-01 time-varying-env hook and mbp-02 population. We recorded 1 finding confirm the expected biology. Gate decision: Not started. Run the baseline simulation to begin evaluation.

Purpose & background (study design)
Question. Can v2ecoli (with the mbp-01 time-varying-env hook and mbp-02 population aggregator) be coupled to `pbg-bioreactordesign`'s BiRDReactorProcess — via a thin adapter that resolves the biomass-ownership conflict between the two — such that BiRD supplies dissolved O2, kLa, gas-phase physics, and v2ecoli supplies population biomass and exchange-flux demand, producing a physically consistent coupled trajectory in a 0D well-mixed bench-scale reactor?
Mechanism / Model change. pbg-bioreactordesign's `BiRDReactorProcess` provides 0D well-mixed reactor physics (Higbie kLa, temperature-dependent Henry's law, Wilke-Chang diffusivity, gas-holdup) but ALSO carries an internal biomass ODE driven by its own Monod kinetics. v2ecoli owns biomass via per-cell mass and Division.

**Option-B resolution (adopted 2026-05-26 per chris_feedback_2026_05_26 §5 + §11; Eran's decision).** Rather than disabling BiRD's internal biomass ODE behind a `bird_disable_internal_biomass=true` flag, fork upstream a new `BiRDTransportProcess` that omits the biomass equation entirely. Rationale: - Substitutability symmetry: the cell-side interface contract makes cell-side engines variable while the reactor side stays fixed; forking gives two reactor variants (with internal biomass for standalone use; without it under the contract). Story symmetric across both sides. - Naming: a `disable X` flag signals "shouldn't be there in the first place" rather than "let users turn it off." - Tested-vs-dead-code paths: with `disable=true` the biomass-ODE code path exists but isn't exercised under this configuration; untested in this regime, no signal if it later quietly breaks.

Done well, Option B is NOT "copy `BiRDReactorProcess` and delete the ODE." It's extract-shared-transport-module — kLa / Henry / Wilke-Chang in a shared module, with `BiRDReactorProcess` and `BiRDTransportProcess` as two consumers (preserves DRY while delivering the design benefit).

**Cross-investigation dependency:** the fork lives upstream in `vivarium-collective/pbg-bioreactordesign`. mbp-03 entering Build phase is BLOCKED on `pbg-bioreactor-transport-fork` (pre-seeded as a candidate-future-study in mbp-06; effectively a hard prereq, see pipeline_gate.prerequisites below).

Coupling actions, given `BiRDTransportProcess`:

(1) **Drive BiRDTransportProcess's biomass-input port with v2ecoli's aggregated population** via a `ReactorCellCoupler` Step that writes `reactor.biomass = population.biomass_concentration_gL` each step. (2) **Drive v2ecoli's environment with BiRD's dissolved-phase**: coupler writes BiRD's `dissolved_o2` / `dissolved_co2` into v2ecoli's `environment.external_concentrations.OXYGEN-MOLECULE[p]` / `CARBON-DIOXIDE[p]` (units conversion mg/L → mM). (3) **Drive BiRD's O2 demand with v2ecoli's metabolism**: coupler aggregates v2ecoli's `external_exchange_fluxes.OXYGEN-MOLECULE[p]` across agents × biomass and writes it as BiRD's `o2_uptake_rate` input. (4) **Drive BiRD's CO2 demand with v2ecoli's metabolism**: symmetric to (3) — `external_exchange_fluxes.CARBON-DIOXIDE[p]` → `co2_production_rate`.

Result: BiRDTransportProcess = transport-only physics; v2ecoli = biology + biomass. The coupling is the minimal adapter on the v2ecoli side; reactor-side cleanup is upstream.
Expected outcome. DO drops below saturation as v2ecoli's population consumes O2; raising kLa raises steady-state DO. Reactor biomass concentration tracks v2ecoli's population growth. With cells removed (population aggregator returning zero), DO converges to BiRD's Henry-saturation. Coupled run completes one v2ecoli generation (~60 min) without state divergence.

Key assumptions

  • 0D well-mixed reactor; bubble column geometry as the default for mbp-03 (per BiRD's default). Stirred-tank may be required for mbp-05 Beulig matching — see open_question reactor-geometry-for-beulig.
  • BiRDTransportProcess (Option-B fork) has no internal biomass ODE; v2ecoli's population is the SOLE source of biomass truth — by construction, not by flag.
  • v2ecoli's per-cell μ from metabolism — when aggregated by cells_per_agent — captures the same physics BiRD's Monod would have approximated.
  • Timestep: sim duration 240 min (4 BiRD ticks at 1-h default) chosen so 'second-half steady-state' windows are meaningful. If BiRD's interval is tunable in the fork (open_question coupler-timestep-tunability), drop to ~minutes and tighten tolerances.

Biology

Carbon ledger: glucose-C in -> biomass-C (~0.46 gC/gDW) + CO2-C (~half of aerobic glucose-C; omitting it is a guaranteed ~50% failure) + acetate/lactate/formate/ethanol/pyruvate/succinate-C (aerobic overflow per Vemuri 2006). Nitrogen ledger (narrow): NH4+ in -> biomass-N (~0.12 gN/gDW). Both residuals expected |<0.02| at every step. Headline observable is the growth->limitation regime transition.

Overview

This study asks whether does the mbp-03 coupled composite (v2ecoli ↔ pbg-bioreactordesign) stay. We recorded 1 novel computational result. Gate decision: Not started. Run the baseline simulation to begin evaluation.

Purpose & background (study design)
Question. Does the mbp-03 coupled composite (v2ecoli ↔ pbg-bioreactordesign) stay mass-conserving, computationally tractable, and physically coherent over multiple v2ecoli generations (3+ doublings) under sustained reactor dynamics — capturing the regime transition from glucose-replete exponential growth into glucose-limited or DO-limited slowdown as the population grows and consumes the batch?
Mechanism / Model change. Take the mbp-03 coupled composite, run for ≥ 3 generations starting from a defined initial glucose pool. As the population grows, glucose drops (via the mbp-01 env hook); as O2 demand grows, DO drops (via the mbp-03 coupler). Eventually one of: (a) glucose depletes → glucose-limited slowdown; (b) DO drops below v2ecoli's metabolism constraint → oxygen-limited slowdown; (c) both. The regime transition is the headline observable.

Mass-balance audit: cumulative glucose decrement = cumulative metabolism glucose uptake integrated over the population. Cell-count audit: cell count over generations matches the integral of μ × population.
Expected outcome. Population grows ~exponentially through the first 2 generations, then flattens as glucose / DO becomes limiting (regime transition near the end of glucose). Carbon and nitrogen mass-balance close to within numerical tolerance. Run completes (no NaN, no infinite loops, no unbounded memory growth) within a wall-clock budget set by the spec PR (target: 3 generations in < 30 min wall time at seed 0).

Population sparsity (chris_feedback_2026_05_26 §10 mbp-04 specifics): mbp-04 inherits the cells_per_agent scaling from mbp-02 (Eran's choice 2026-05-26). Production runs of three-generation-batch should set cells_per_agent such that initial biomass concentration is in the glucose-depletion-feasible range (target ~0.01-0.1 gDW/L initial so 4 g/L glucose depletes within the 240-min sim window). At literal-sum (cells_per_agent=1.0), the population cannot deplete a 4 g/L pool in 240 min — the regime-transition test premise wouldn't resolve. See open_question glucose-pool-sizing for the calibration discipline.

req-1-mass-balance-auditorMassBalanceAuditor StepprocessSopen
PBG Step that integrates external-pool decrements, biomass accumulation, metabolism exchange-flux outputs, and gas-phase transfer (via the BiRD coupler diagnostics) to compute carbon/nitrogen mass-balance residuals. Reads cumulative tracker…
Unblocks:
  • carbon-mass-balance-closes-over-3-generations
  • nitrogen-mass-balance-closes-over-3-generations
Implementation detailPBG Step that integrates external-pool decrements, biomass accumulation, metabolism exchange-flux outputs, and gas-phase transfer (via the BiRD coupler diagnostics) to compute carbon/nitrogen mass-balance residuals. Reads cumulative trackers exposed by EnvironmentDriver and PopulationAggregator. Writes reactor.diagnostics.{carbon,nitrogen}_residual.

**EXPLICIT required-tracked species (chris_feedback_2026_05_26 §9 — must be in the auditor design, not just in failure_modes as candidate causes):**

Carbon ledger (target tolerance 2% — only tractable if CO2 + acetate explicitly bookkept): - Glucose decrement (external pool, via EnvironmentDriver cumulative tracker) - Biomass carbon accumulation (∫ μ × biomass × C_coefficient × dt; C_coefficient ≈ 0.46 gC/gDW for E. coli) - **CO2-C** evolved by metabolism (∫ metabolism CO2 exchange flux × biomass × dt; flows out via gas-liquid transfer per BiRD coupler). Roughly half of glucose-C consumed under aerobic growth; missing it is a guaranteed 50% C-balance failure, NOT a small error mode. - **Acetate-C** and other byproduct organic acids (∫ metabolism ACET/LAC/FOR/PYR/SUCC exchange fluxes × biomass × dt). v2ecoli produces acetate under aerobic overflow per Vemuri 2006; the C-balance must track it.

Nitrogen ledger (target tolerance 2% — pool defined narrowly so the tolerance is achievable): - **N-pool definition:** NH4+ exchange flux + biomass-N. EXCLUDES intermediate amino acids / peptides / nucleotides (which sum to << 2% under steady-state turnover). - NH4+ decrement (external pool, via EnvironmentDriver) - Biomass nitrogen accumulation (∫ μ × biomass × N_coefficient × dt; N_coefficient ≈ 0.12 gN/gDW for E. coli)

Residual computation: carbon_residual = (Σ inputs - Σ outputs - Δ biomass-C) / Σ inputs nitrogen_residual = (Σ inputs - Σ outputs - Δ biomass-N) / Σ inputs

Both should be |residual| < 0.02 at every emit step over the run.

Limitations

  • Batch only; fed-batch operations require either an upstream pbg-bioreactordesign enhancement or a v2ecoli-side feed Step — deferred (candidate-future-study; see mbp-06).
  • Single seed; stochastic variation across seeds not characterized here (a candidate-future-study). Cells_per_agent scaling further washes per-seed stochastic variance — explicit cost of the mbp-02 architectural choice.
  • Bubble column geometry; stirred tank / airlift not validated.
  • Acetate (+ lactate / formate / ethanol / pyruvate / succinate) handling depends on v2ecoli's metabolism; the MassBalanceAuditor explicitly tracks each species (req-1) but biological correctness of the production rates is not separately validated this phase.
  • Population uses cells_per_agent scaling (mbp-02) to make 240-min batch dynamics resolvable. At scaling factors k ≥ ~1e6, per-cell stochastic variance washes out at the bulk mean — correct biology at high density, but obscures per-cell heterogeneity that may matter for Beulig's bistable-expression regimes. Surrogate engine remains the path for the full high-density regime (mbp-06).

Overview

This study asks whether configured with operating conditions matched to the 2025 Palsson lab. We recorded 1 novel computational result. Gate decision: Not started. Run the baseline simulation to begin evaluation.

Purpose & background (study design)
Question. Configured with operating conditions matched to the 2025 Palsson lab high-density E. coli study, does the v2ecoli ↔ pbg-bioreactordesign coupled model **render a structured comparison report** (sim-vs- published overlays + categorized divergences + open questions) on the published WT batch-phase prefix trajectories, suitable to feed mbp-06's gap-analysis synthesis?

Investigation-level note: the original question framing ("match within tolerance") was reframed 2026-05-26 to "render a structured comparison." The success definition is whether the comparison was EXECUTED AND REPORTED COHERENTLY, not whether biology matched. All biological divergences feed mbp-06 unchanged.
Mechanism / Model change. The benchmark paper is Beulig et al. 2025 (mSystems 10(7), doi:10.1128/msystems.00323-25; senior author B. Palsson), titled "Trade-off between resistance and persistence in high cell density cultures." Open access, PDF at `references/papers/Beulig_2025_mSystems_high_cell_density.pdf`; extracted metadata + scope notes at `references/expert/palsson_2025_fed_batch.md`. Digitized trajectories at `references/papers/palsson-2025-supp/`.

Two-stage batch → fed-batch fermentation to 50–80 gDW/L in parallel well-controlled bioreactors; exponential feeding after batch-to-fed- batch transition (t=0 h); >470 transcriptomic samples across five strain groups (WT BW25113, 31 SGKO, TRP, TRPp, MEL) and four fermentation phases (I–IV).

For mbp-05, scope is WT only and (until fed-batch lands in pbg-bioreactordesign) the BATCH PHASE PREFIX. Configure the mbp-03/04 coupled composite to the published operating profile (reactor geometry, aeration, medium, initial conditions). Run; render comparison overlays for every sim ↔ published trajectory pair listed in `comparison_overlays` below (~8 surfaces); categorize divergences in the report card across four categories (v2ecoli metabolic deficiency / coupling-adapter limitation / experimental uncertainty / placeholder-induced).

**No new model capability.** model_change is empty. The comparison harness (`req-2-comparison-harness`) is generic over the `comparison_overlays` config — adding a new comparison = adding one YAML entry. Future investigations reuse the harness with their own list.

Transcriptional-state matching against the >470 transcriptomes is a natural extension (v2ecoli outputs transcript counts) — out of mbp-05 scope; pre-seeded as mbp-09 candidate-future-study in mbp-06.
Expected outcome. For each entry in `comparison_overlays`, the harness produces a single overlay panel + derived comparison metrics. The deliverable is the report card: a markdown document with all overlay panels and a structured `## Divergence triage` section enumerating divergences against the four-category taxonomy, each pointing at the specific sim path / published column / observation that drove the categorization.

Pass / fail of each test below is about whether the overlay+triage artifact was produced — not whether biology matched. Divergences are valuable: each one is a specific mbp-06 gap finding seed.

Visualisations from the latest run

v2ecoli vs Beulig 2025 batch-phase biomass-density gap (preliminary)⚠ stale
Final biomass concentration (g/L) from existing mbp-02 multigen runs at cpa ∈ {1, 1e6, 1e9}, overlaid against Beulig 2025 batch-phase target band (50-80 g/L). Star marks the cpa that would close the residual gap at the current 2-gen / 60-sim-min batch duration: ~2e+13.
Simulations behind this chart. aggregator-cpa1/1e6/1e9-multigen (mbp-02 v2-parquet hives, seed=0).
What it means. cpa=1 (literal single-cell) reaches ~3.3e-12 g/L at t=2-gen. cpa=1e9 (Beulig-regime representative-sampling) reaches ~3.3e-03 g/L — still 4.2 orders below Beulig's stated 50-80 g/L target. The residual gap is NOT a cpa-scaling problem (cpa is exact, see chart 04 variance bands); it's a BATCH-DURATION problem. v2ecoli's current 60-sim-min / 2-gen runs are far short of Beulig's ~6 h batch phase. Closing the gap requires (a) longer batch duration to accumulate more cell mass per agent, (b) cpa ~ 2e+13 (near Avogadro-mol scale — likely impractical), OR (c) fed-batch operations (deferred upstream blocker, pbg-bioreactor-transport-fork). mbp-05's comparison harness can render this gap explicitly BEFORE evaluating whether v2ecoli's biology reproduces Beulig's trajectory — diagnostic-first, evaluative-second.
Biomass trajectories (cpa=1/1e6/1e9) vs Beulig 2025 batch endpoint⚠ stale
log-y population.biomass_concentration_gL(t) for cpa ∈ {1, 1e6, 1e9} v2ecoli runs alongside Beulig 2025's batch-phase endpoint band at t=6h. Time-series counterpart to chart 00.
Simulations behind this chart. aggregator-cpa1/1e6/1e9-multigen (60 sim-min, 2 gen, seed=0).
What it means. Visual rendering of the 4-5 order density-gap at the same time-axis as Beulig's batch endpoint. v2ecoli's 60-min trajectories end far below Beulig's 6-h endpoint band, and the slopes don't suggest the gap would close with a 6x duration extension — per-cell mass plateaus after ~1 generation in the M9-glucose calibration regime. Closing the gap needs the architectural moves listed in chart 00's meta (longer duration via fed-batch / impossibly-large cpa / candidate surrogate engine in mbp-06).
v2ecoli plateau vs Beulig 2025 batch trajectories (preliminary, refined)⚠ stale
log-y biomass(t) — v2ecoli at cpa=1e9 at two durations (60-sim-min reference + 175-sim-min salvaged from a 6h sim killed at the memory wall) overlaid against the 5 best-sampled Beulig reactors' batch-phase trajectories. The 175-min run confirms v2ecoli's biomass plateaus around 4.3 mg/L per division cycle, NOT because duration is short but because single_daughters caps total biomass at cell_mass × cpa for one lineage.
Simulations behind this chart. v2ecoli: aggregator-cpa1e9-multigen (seed=0, 60 sim-min, gen 1-2) + aggregator-cpa1e9-batch-prefix-multigen (seed=0, salvaged 175 sim-min from a 6h run terminated at the 128GB memory ceiling). Beulig: DDB_PD_006_AMBR_R9, DDB_PD_009_AMBR_R10, DDB_PD_009_AMBR_R11, DDB_PD_006_AMBR_R8, DDB_PD_038_AMBR_R10 from reactor_OD_data.csv, batch phase only.
What it means. This chart settles the architectural question conclusively. v2ecoli at cpa=1e9 plateaus around 4.3 mg/L over 175 sim-min — the trajectory oscillates between ~1 and ~4 mg/L following the division cycle (cell_mass 1100→2300 fg → halve at division), but does NOT accumulate across generations. The single_daughters convention follows ONE lineage; biomass = cell_mass × cpa is bounded by the cell's mass range. Beulig batch peaks at ~9.6 g/L — 3.3 orders above v2ecoli's plateau. Closing this gap requires either: (a) a population composite that tracks accumulating cell count (counter to single_daughters), (b) impossibly-large cpa (~1e12), or (c) fed-batch + surrogate engine (mbp-06 candidate-future-study). mbp-05's comparison harness will surface this diagnostically rather than try to close it via tuning. [2026-05-29 CAVEAT — single_daughters configuration]: This chart's plateau finding is empirically valid FOR the single_daughters configuration (one daughter followed at each division — the v2ecoli default). The architectural-cap statement is overstated as a blanket claim: with both daughters tracked (--no-single-daughters), v2ecoli's population doubles every generation and biomass DOES accumulate exponentially. The follow-up run aggregator-cpa1e9-multigen --no-single-daughters tests this directly; see chart 03 (companion). The 3.3-order single_daughters plateau gap may be reduced to ~1.2 orders under both_daughters, though full closure to Beulig batch (~9.6 g/L) still requires fed-batch operations + the architectural decisions in mbp-06.
single_daughters vs --no-single-daughters: empirical plateau comparison⚠ stale
log-y biomass(t) for two cpa=1e9 runs differing only in the runner's lineage flag: single_daughters (175 sim-min, the v2ecoli default) and --no-single-daughters (90 sim-min). Both peak at ~4.4 mg/L despite the runner config difference.
Simulations behind this chart. aggregator-cpa1e9-batch-prefix-multigen (sim_id ee0a02b0, single_daughters=True, 175 sim-min) + aggregator-cpa1e9-multigen --no-single-daughters (sim_id 404f89f0, 90 sim-min, max_gen=3). Both at seed=0, cpa=1e9, baseline_population composite.
What it means. REVISES chart-02's architectural-cap framing with EMPIRICAL evidence. The both-daughters run peaks at 4.39 mg/L (Δ +2.1% vs single_daughters' 4.31 mg/L). The runner's INTERNAL log line `gen 2 → following agent '00' at tick 2501` reveals the root cause: `run_multigen_parquet` (v2ecoli.library.parquet_run) simulates BOTH daughters at division moments but then follows ONE lineage for continued simulation + parquet emission. So `--no-single-daughters` flips the COMPOSITE-LEVEL division behavior but doesn't change the runner's emit pattern, and the plateau persists. The chart 02 architectural claim about single_daughters capping biomass at cell_mass × cpa is true for OBSERVED biomass but the actual root cause is the runner's lineage-emit logic, NOT the single_daughters config alone. For TRUE both-daughters accumulation (2^N cells after N gens), v2ecoli needs a fundamentally different runner that simulates all agents in parallel — neither single_daughters=True/False in the current run_multigen_parquet path produces it. This is itself an architectural finding for mbp-06: 'population composite runner' as a candidate-future-study, distinct from the single_daughters lineage convention. Closing the Beulig batch gap (~9.6 g/L) still requires fed-batch + that population-runner architecture, not just a config flip.

Implementation detailIterates over the study's `comparison_overlays` list, for each entry: - Resolves `sim_path` against the run output (handles `aggregation: per_biomass` and any other reductions). - Loads `published_csv` and extracts `published_column`. - Renders an overlay panel (sim trajectory + published trajectory, time-aligned) → report/overlay_<name>.png - Computes per-overlay derived metrics (end-of-run value diff, shape-similarity, peak timing, etc. — keyed by the panel's `backs_tests`). - Categorizes any large divergences into the four-axis taxonomy in report/divergence_triage.md (with evidence pointer to the panel + sim_path + published_column). The harness is GENERIC: adding a new comparison surface = adding one `comparison_overlays` entry. No code change. Future investigations reuse the harness with their own `comparison_overlays` list.

Limitations

  • EVALUATION PHASE (chris_feedback_2026_05_26 §10): mbp-05 deliberately does NOT make tolerance-based biology claims. The original framing (`end-of-run-od-matches-published` etc.) structurally encoded an open-ended menu of model knobs to turn — even with the 'no silent tuning' discipline, the impulse to tune to a tolerance-test was built into the test design. The reframe shifts the bound on the AI agent to 'execute and report'.
  • Single benchmark study; not a multi-dataset validation.
  • Fed-batch operations remain a deferred enhancement (pbg-bioreactordesign has no fed-batch yet); this study scopes to the BATCH-PHASE PREFIX of the Beulig dataset.
  • v2ecoli's calibration is slow-growth M9-glucose (~60-min doubling, single cell); the high-density 50–80 gDW/L regime is OUTSIDE the calibration envelope. Under the new framing this is no longer a 'tolerance must reflect this' caveat — it becomes one of the divergences mbp-06's gap analysis categorizes.
  • Strain scope: WT BW25113 only. SGKO (31 knockouts) / TRP / TRPp / MEL are deferred — natural candidate-future-studies under v2ecoli's variant scope.
  • Transcriptional-state matching against >470 Beulig transcriptomes is a unique benchmark axis (v2ecoli has transcripts; upstream dFBA path does not) — deferred to mbp-09 (pre-seeded in mbp-06).

Biology

Not a biological-mechanism study. It catalogs where the investigation's biology coverage is incomplete: e.g. v2ecoli PTS transport functional form (axis A), low-GUR mass balance during substrate depletion (axis A), cells_per_agent stochastic-floor at high density vs Beulig's bistable expression states (axis A), and the v2ecoli-vs-Beulig batch-density gap surfaced by mbp-05 (architectural, not tuning). These are inputs to the triage, not new findings.

Overview

This study asks whether after mbp-01..05 have produced their per-study findings, what are the. Gate decision: In progress. Continue analysing run outcomes.

Purpose & background (study design)
Question. After mbp-01..05 have produced their per-study findings, what are the remaining gaps (in v2ecoli's biology coverage, the coupling layer, the pbg-bioreactordesign physics, and the Beulig benchmark scope) that prevent the investigation from answering its overarching question, and how should those gaps be prioritized as the next investigation iteration (mbp-* round 2, or a sibling investigation)?
Mechanism / Model change. No new simulation. The study WALKS the prior-study artifacts: every behavior_test's outcome, every recorded finding, every limitation / open_question / candidate-future-study pointer. It synthesizes these into a structured gap-analysis covering five named axes:

A. **v2ecoli biology coverage** — places where v2ecoli's metabolism / regulation / mass machinery is insufficient for the reactor regime (e.g. low-DO acetate overflow strength, high-density maintenance re-allocation per Beulig 2025). B. **Coupling layer** — limitations of the v2ecoli ↔ pbg-bioreactor- design adapter (biomass-ownership disable, timestep mismatch, single-cell-with-Division ceiling). C. **pbg-bioreactordesign physics** — what BiRD doesn't yet model (fed-batch operations, multi-stream feeds, pH-CO2 coupling). D. **Beulig benchmark scope** — what was deferred from mbp-05 (SGKO / TRP / MEL strain extension, transcriptional-state matching against >470 transcriptomes, fed-batch phases I–IV). E. **Methodology** — places where the biological-BDD discipline (claims → tests → triage) didn't catch a gap soon enough, or where the cell-side interface contract needs revision based on what was learned.

For each gap, the study records: signature, evidence (which test(s) / finding(s) surfaced it), severity (blocks-next-step | reduces-coverage | open-question), candidate-resolution (a new study slug, an upstream PR to pbg-bioreactordesign, an expert elicitation), and priority (1–3).
Expected outcome. A structured findings document (findings.md + this study's `findings.entries[]`, populated post-impl) that enumerates ≥ 8 named gaps across the five axes (with per-axis floors: ≥ 3 on axes A and D based on prior known limitations), each with a concrete candidate_resolution AND with the extended schema fields below (chris_feedback_2026_05_26 §11 concern 2):

- resolution_type: model_improvement | scope_decision | upstream_PR | expert_elicitation | further_investigation - resolution_venue: <repo / sibling investigation / program-level decision> - decision_authority: <who decides — especially for scope_decision> - provenance: this_investigation | carried_prior | external_input | expert_elicitation - priority: 1 (top) | 2 | 3 - evidence: [list of upstream test results / limitations / open_questions / mandatory_findings_to_consider entries]

Priorities are assigned INDEPENDENTLY of provenance — a carried prior can be priority 1 even if mbp-05 didn't surface it fresh.

The document feeds the next investigation cycle: roadmap-revision PR on references/expert/multiscale_bioprocess_roadmap.md (if upstream) + new study scaffolds for the prioritized gaps.

Prerequisites: none (root study)

Enables: —

Proceed when: Gap-analysis covers all 5 axes (A–E); each gap has a concrete candidate-resolution; priorities are assigned and reviewed by the expert / user. The document is committed to findings.md and the candidate-resolution slugs are reified as scaffolded follow-up studies OR explicit "deferred" entries in the next roadmap revision.

If primary tests pass: All five axes covered with per-axis floors met (A6/B2/C2/D3/E2), every gap carries a resolution_type+venue (+decision_authority for scope_decision), a provenance, and all four mandatory carried priors are incorporated -> the gap taxonomy is accepted as the next-iteration roadmap. Drive the next cycle from the priority-1 gaps: the both-daughters population runner + fed-batch (batch-scale architectural gap), Millard kinetic calibration to division, and the pbg-bioreactordesign fed-batch PR.
If primary tests fail: If an axis floor is unmet or a gap lacks a resolution/provenance, the synthesis is incomplete: re-walk the upstream mbp-01..07 limitations/open_questions and the beulig_batch report cards for the missed axis before locking the taxonomy (see failure_modes).

Overview

This study asks whether the Millard kinetic-metabolism arc, end-to-end. Can the Millard 2017. We recorded 1 novel computational result. Gate decision: Not started. Run the baseline simulation to begin evaluation.

Purpose & background (study design)
Question. The Millard kinetic-metabolism arc, end-to-end. Can the Millard 2017 kinetic central-carbon ODE replace v2ecoli's constraint-based central- carbon FBA as a drop-in cell engine under the cell-side interface contract?

Three linked questions: 1. BUILD — does the swapped composite (baseline_millard) build and run, with non-trivial live central fluxes (kinetic ODE active, not FBA)? 2. VALIDATE — does the Millard whole-cell model recover growth comparable to the FBA baseline, and (once the Millard cell exposes mass-exchange accounting) close mass conservation? 3. COMPARE — coupled to the same BiRD reactor and run against the Beulig WT batch prefix, does the Millard kinetic central metabolism track the bioreactor (growth, substrate, gas transfer) BETTER than v2ecoli's WCM-FBA — and how do both compare to the iML1515 genome-scale FBA (Palsson)? Rendered as a structured 3-arm report-card comparison (per-group axis verdicts + categorized divergences), NOT a tolerance gate (execute-and-report, per chris_feedback_2026_05_26 §10).

Visualizations

Metabolism-swap growth — cell_mass + central fluxes under Millard (interactive)

baseline_millard, 60 steps: cell_mass and live Millard central-carbon fluxes with the kinetic ODE replacing FBA. Hover/zoom; toggle fluxes.

Millard env-responsiveness — PTS uptake vs external glucose (interactive)

Glucose sweep: the Millard PTS uptake flux responds to external glucose (0.05 to 50 mM), confirming the kinetic arm is environment-coupled.

Build / fix list (3)

Concrete engineering work to fully exercise this study.

req-1-millard-exchange-accountingMillard cell exposes O2/CO2 exchange to the reactor couplerprocessMdone
The Millard cell (baseline_millard) replaced FBA metabolism, so it does NOT populate `agents.*.environment.exchange` with O2/CO2 — which is what ReactorCellCoupler reads to drive reactor consumption. Without this the Millard-coupled reactor…
Unblocks:
  • the Millard arm + wcm-mass-conservation-closes-millard on baseline_millard
Implementation detailThe Millard cell (baseline_millard) replaced FBA metabolism, so it does NOT populate `agents.*.environment.exchange` with O2/CO2 — which is what ReactorCellCoupler reads to drive reactor consumption. Without this the Millard-coupled reactor is degenerate (cell consumes no reactor O2; DO stays at saturation). The Millard 2017 model HAS an O2 species + central fluxes, so translate Millard's O2 uptake / CO2 evolution (central_fluxes) into the cell- side exchange the coupler consumes (counts into environment.exchange, or a Millard-aware coupler input). This is the deferred Millard mass-exchange accounting (also unblocks the wcm-mass-conservation gate on the Millard cell).
req-2-millard-coupled-compositereactor_bird_coupled (Millard variant)compositeSdone
A composite coupling baseline_millard (instead of baseline_population's FBA cell) to BiRDTransportHours + ReactorCellCoupler — i.e. the mbp-03 wiring with the Millard cell engine swapped in (the cell-side interface contract makes this a dro…
Implementation detailA composite coupling baseline_millard (instead of baseline_population's FBA cell) to BiRDTransportHours + ReactorCellCoupler — i.e. the mbp-03 wiring with the Millard cell engine swapped in (the cell-side interface contract makes this a drop-in). Likely a `cell_engine` param on reactor_bird_coupled, or a sibling reactor_bird_coupled_millard.
req-3-beulig-report-cardReuse the mbp-05 Beulig comparison harness for all armsharnessMopen
Run the arms against the Beulig batch prefix through the mbp-05 comparison harness, producing a report_card_verdict.json per arm at the card paths below, so the report_card_axis tests grade them. Reuses mbp-05's comparison_overlays + grader…
Implementation detailRun the arms against the Beulig batch prefix through the mbp-05 comparison harness, producing a report_card_verdict.json per arm at the card paths below, so the report_card_axis tests grade them. Reuses mbp-05's comparison_overlays + grader (req: mbp-05 built). Now covers THREE arms — the Millard kinetic cell (millard_vs_beulig), the WCM-FBA cell (vs_beulig), and the iML1515 genome-scale FBA contrast (iml1515_vs_beulig).

How the verdict is computed — acceptance criteria & gating matrix
AC → study gating matrix which study gates each acceptance criterion · ⚠ = no study linked (gap)

Each acceptance criterion is a behaviour test declared in a study: a measured field from the run (e.g. closure_gap_size) compared against an explicit pass_if band (a numeric threshold/range). The per-criterion result, each study’s gate verdict, and this roll-up are computed in code from the run outcomes (deterministic) — not human judgement. Expand a row to see the field, the passing band, and the observed value.

Acceptance criterionGating studyResult
all-five-axes-covered
field structural_count_per_axis · passes if {"op":"per_axis_at_least"}
Each of the five gap axes (v2ecoli biology / coupling / BiRD physics / Beulig scope / methodology) has at least one named gap entry. Per-axis floors (chris_feedback_2026_05_26 §11 tactical): axes A and D ≥ 3 each (based on prior known limitations); axes B, C, E ≥ 1 each.
mbp-06-gap-analysis◐ in-progress
every-gap-has-candidate-resolution
field structural_check · passes if {"op":"all_pass"}
Every gap entry carries a non-empty `candidate_resolution.target_slug` OR `candidate_resolution.venue` (for resolution_types where no follow-up slug applies: scope_decision, expert_elicitation). Placeholder / unresolved values are banned (case-insensitive): the canonical placeholder tokens flagged by the workspace report-linter, plus the study-specific phrases enumerated in `measure.banned_strings` below (e.g. "to be determined", "figure out later", "unclear", "n/a").
mbp-06-gap-analysis◐ in-progress
divergences-categorized-in-report-card
field structural_check · passes if {"op":"all_pass"}
Divergences categorized in the report card across the four-category taxonomy (v2ecoli metabolic deficiency / coupling-adapter limitation / experimental uncertainty / placeholder-induced). Each divergence entry references the specific overlay panel + sim path + published column that drove the categorization, suitable for direct ingestion as a mbp-06 gap finding seed.
mbp-05-palsson-benchmark◐ in-progress
external_glucose_updates_propagate_within_one_step
field one_step_propagation · passes if propagates_within 1
An external_glucose store update is reflected in metabolism's GLC[p] exchange constraint within one timestep. Direct wire check — replaces the removed `uptake-flux-tracks-external-glucose` Pearson test (which assumed linear response between concentration and uptake; v2ecoli's PTS is saturable).
mbp-01-time-varying-environment◐ in-progress
cumulative-mass-balance-closes
field derived · passes if in [0, 0.05]
Closed-balance cumulative mass conservation (MassConservationDeriver) — the relative cumulative residual between cell-mass change and net environmental exchange stays near zero, confirming the environment hook is wired without leakage.
mbp-01-time-varying-environment◐ in-progress
zero-substrate-blocks-uptake
field multi_path_max_abs · passes if at_most 0.01
external_glucose held at 0 → glucose exchange flux ≈ 0 (numerical tolerance). Same for DO: zero external DO → O2 exchange flux ≈ 0. Universal biological floor; also confirms plumbing.
mbp-01-time-varying-environment◐ in-progress
saturating-substrate-respects-vmax
field series · passes if at_most 12
external_glucose held at 50 g/L (~30,000× PTS Km) → glucose exchange flux ≤ published Vmax for E. coli glucose-PTS (~10–12 mmol/gDW/h). Catches the unphysical linear-scaling implementation case.
mbp-01-time-varying-environment◐ in-progress
plateau-across-saturating-range
field cross_run_ratio · passes if in [0.9, 1.1]
Two runs at 5 g/L and 50 g/L (both far above PTS Km) → GUR within a tight ratio tolerance. Both above Km, so saturable and constant-bound models predict matching GUR; linear scaling would predict ~10× difference. Direct discriminator between physical and unphysical implementations.
mbp-01-time-varying-environment◐ in-progress
cell-count-doubles-per-generation
field derived_ratio · passes if in [6, 24]
cell_count doubles approximately every doubling-time (~60 min on M9-glucose); ratio (final/initial) ≈ 2^(duration/doubling_time). Implicitly assumes calibrated v2ecoli baseline μ as a fixed prior — drift in this test should first prompt a baseline-composite drift check, not just an aggregator check.
mbp-02-population-aggregation◐ in-progress
per-cell-observables-unchanged-vs-baseline
field trajectory_match · passes if {"op":"distribution_match","tolerance":0.05}
Per-cell DnaA count distribution matches the unaggregated v2ecoli baseline — aggregation is purely additive, doesn't perturb cell state. Regression guard.
mbp-02-population-aggregation◐ in-progress
population_count_equals_len_agents
field per_step_identity · passes if {"op":"identity_at_every_step"}
At every emit step: population.cell_count == len(agents.*) × cells_per_agent. Pure aggregator-only check; independent of doubling-time calibration.
mbp-02-population-aggregation◐ in-progress
total_biomass_equals_sum_cell_mass_times_scale
field per_step_identity · passes if {"op":"identity_at_every_step","rtol":"1e-9"}
At every emit step: population.total_biomass_gDW == sum(agents.*.listeners.mass.cell_mass) × cells_per_agent × 1e-15. Pure aggregator-only check; isolates aggregation bugs from biology drift.
mbp-02-population-aggregation◐ in-progress
one-generation-completes-without-divergence
field completion_check · passes if {"op":"all_pass"}
Coupled sim runs for one v2ecoli doubling time (60 min) without state divergence (no NaN; DO stays in [0, saturation]; cell_count ≥ 1).
mbp-03-bird-reactor-coupling◐ in-progress
cells-drop-do-below-saturation
field derived_difference · passes if at_most 0
With v2ecoli cells consuming O2, steady-state dissolved O2 sits below BiRD's Henry-law saturation.

higher-kla-raises-steady-state-do

o2-mass-balance-closes

Cumulative O2 consumed by v2ecoli (∫ metabolism O2 flux × biomass × dt) + dissolved-O2 change in the reactor ≈ kLa-driven gas-liquid transfer integrated over the run (∫ kLa × (saturation - dissolved) × volume × dt).
